::: {#b20 .paragraph bbox="194 1393 1494 1511"}
Areas under the normal curve are available in tables, and Excel also provides a method to find these areas. The [empirical rule]{.term} is one method for determining areas under the normal curve that fall within a certain number of standard deviations of the mean (see Figure 13.4).
:::

::: {#b22 .caption of=b21 label="Figure 13.4" bbox="397 1861 1296 1902"}
Figure 13.4 Normal Distribution Showing Mean and Increments of Standard Deviation
:::

::: {#b23 .description of=b21 form=prose}
A symmetric bell-shaped curve over a horizontal axis labelled x. Dashed vertical lines rise from the axis at the mean μ and at one, two and three standard deviations either side of it (−3σ to 3σ). The curve peaks at μ and is almost flat beyond ±3σ.
:::
